content.title: The trends behind Karol Nawrocki's Polish election win
content.lead: Young men and a bit of help from Donald Trump? National conservative Karol Nawrocki won a narrow victory in Sunday's presidential election. Maps and charts explain four key insights from the results.
content.author: Eike Hoppmann

content.html:
Summary

  • Karol Nawrocki narrowly won the Polish presidential election against Rafał Trzaskowski, with rural areas and younger men playing a crucial role.
  • Geographic and demographic analyses reveal an East-West divide: Nawrocki dominated in the country's southeast, while Trzaskowski led in cities and the northwest.
  • Polish voters abroad were also divided. Those in Europe largely supported Trzaskowski, while Nawrocki came out ahead in North America. Overall, voter turnout reached a record high of 71%.

content.text: It has never been so close: 1.8 percentage points, or the equivalent of just under 370,000 votes, decided the outcome of the presidential election in Poland . Karol Nawrocki , supported by the national conservative Law and Justice Party (PiS), prevailed over Rafał Trzaskowski , who belongs to Prime Minister Donald Tusk's liberal pro-European Civic Platform.

content.text: Polish society seems to be split into two roughly equal camps. Data analysis of the election results shows what may have tipped the scales in Nawrocki's favor.

content.title: The northwest and the cities voted for Trzaskowski, the rest for Nawrocki.

content.text: Two geographical patterns can be seen in the election results: First, Trzaskowski, who is the mayor of Warsaw, won in the capital and other urban areas. Nawrocki won over voters in rural areas.

content.text: Second, there is an east-west divide. The national conservative PiS party has its strongholds in the southeast of the country (colored blue), which is more Catholic and has an older population. The northwest, on the other hand, is more liberal (orange). This divide is not new; Poland has been voting along the former pre-World War I borders for decades.

content.title: Men and younger people vote more to the right

content.text: Although the two candidates received almost the same number of votes, there are differences: Men preferred to vote for the former boxer and soccer hooligan Nawrocki. He was 10 percentage points ahead among this group of voters.

content.text: Among older voters, Trzaskowski and Nawrocki were roughly neck and neck. The younger ones, however, had a clear favorite: Nawrocki, the future president. However, Nawrocki was not the first choice among young men. In the first round, most of them voted for the far-right politician Sławomir Mentzen , who came in third but failed to make it to the runoff.

content.text: This is consistent with developments in other countries: across Europe younger voters, especially male voters, are increasingly turning to parties to the right of the political center. In the German federal election in February, the Alternative for Germany (AfD) became the second strongest party among voters under 25 .

content.title: Poles living abroad in Europe voted for Trzaskowski, while in North America, Trump supporter Nawrocki won more votes.

content.text: Given how close the result was, the 600,000 votes cast by Poles living abroad were also significant. Poles living abroad voted for Trzaskowski in all European countries with at least 1,000 valid votes. Even in Hungary, where Nawrocki sought to align himself with Prime Minister Viktor Orban during the election campaign, the liberal candidate was ahead.

Only in North America is the pattern different. In the US, Nawrocki came out on top with 56.6% of the vote to 43.5%. President Donald Trump has publicly supported him and even welcomed him to the White House during the election campaign.

content.title: Poles knew how important the election was – and flocked to the polls.

content.text: The choice between Nawrocki and Trzaskowski was seen as a decision that could shape the country's future direction and have an impact on foreign policy: under Nawrocki, Poland could move closer to Trump's US and distance itself from its European partners. The Polish people also seemed to be aware of the significance of the election: voter turnout was over 71%, a record high for a presidential election.

metadata.nzzSummaryEN:
- Karol Nawrocki narrowly won Poland's presidential election by just 1.8 percentage points over Rafał Trzaskowski. Nawrocki was backed by the national conservative PiS party, while Trzaskowski represented the pro-European Civic Platform.
- The election revealed clear geographical and demographic divides: Nawrocki excelled in rural areas and the southeast, while Trzaskowski led in cities and the northwest. Young men increasingly lean to the right.
- Polish expatriates in Europe favored Trzaskowski, whereas Nawrocki performed better in North America, benefiting from Donald Trump's endorsement. Voter turnout exceeded 71%, marking a record high.
metadata.nzzSummaryDE:
Karol Nawrocki won the narrow Polish presidential election by just 1.8 percentage points over Rafał Trzaskowski. He was supported by the national-conservative Law and Justice party (PiS), while Trzaskowski was backed by the pro-European Civic Platform.
 The election revealed a clear geographical and demographic divide: Nawrocki dominated in rural areas and the southeast, while Trzaskowski found more support in cities and the northwest. Young men, in particular, are increasingly leaning to the right.
 Polish voters abroad in Europe preferred Trzaskowski, while Nawrocki led in North America, thanks to support from Donald Trump. Voter turnout was record-breakingly high at over 71%.
